stem: Which term describes a morphological defect resulting from an extrinsic mechanical force, such as $oligo$ $hydramnios$ or a large uterine fibroid, acting upon a normally developing structure?
explanation: This occurs when physical forces distort or alter the shape of a body part that was otherwise forming correctly.
rationale: This concept involves the physical molding of a structure by its environment rather than a cellular defect.

optionExplanations.A: This refers to a primary defect in the actual formation of an anatomical structure during organogenesis.
optionExplanations.B: This occurs when physical forces distort or alter the shape of a body part that was otherwise forming correctly.
optionExplanations.C: This involves a destructive process that breaks down or fuzes structures after they have already developed.
optionExplanations.D: This term specifically describes the abnormal organization or arrangement of cells within a tissue.

source.hint: This concept involves the physical molding of a structure by its environment rather than a cellular defect.
